messages:
alex: heads-up — NF4 canary (canary-pool-7) shows a ~20% drop in token throughput and a sharp memory spike on host gpu-7c. started right after the new calibration sweep landed at 03:12UTC. logs attached below.

jia: ugh. do we have perf profiles? p95/p99 change? any change in sequence length distribution from traffic?

alex: p95 latency up ~40ms, p99 noisy. throughput metric (tokens/s) down 18-22% across the pool. request size distro looks same (mostly <=512). included tail of the raw log:

alex: ```
[03:13:04] model=nf4-v2 kernel=4bit-opt batch=auto kv_cache_evictions=high host=gpu-7c
[03:13:04] mem.used_before=7.2GB mem.used_after=11.6GB delta=4.4GB
[03:13:04] dropped_requests=0 backpressure=1 latency_ms=162
[03:13:10] scheduler=continuous_batcher window_ms=12 -> ramping to 32
```

perf-bot: automated profile for gpu-7c (03:12-03:18):
perf-bot: ```
- kernel_time% increased for softmax/transpose kernels by ~12%
- L2 miss rate +8% compared to baseline
- stall_cycles due to mem_barrier +15%
```

rowan: ok interesting. hypothesis: the NF4 calibration increased per-token KV footprint slightly for certain seqs, which pushes a few slots over the eviction threshold. eviction/hysteresis policy then thrashes — frequent evict/reload -> more mem traffic -> slow softmax/transpose kernels. also continuous batching window ramping to 32 increases concurrency so more KV pressure at once.

maria: do we have the KV eviction counters broken down by model version? can we correlate which shards are affected?

alex: yes, grabbed per-shard counters:
alex: ```
shard-3: evict_count=3123 reload_count=3098 evict_ratio=0.997
shard-7: evict_count=210 reload_count=207 evict_ratio=0.986
shard-3 hot sequences were mostly <256 but some 1024 requests caused big jumps
```

rowan: evict_ratio ~1 is the smoking gun. hysteresis window is 5MB right now; if calibration bumps kv by ~4MB for some rows they flip back and forth. suggested quick mitigation: increase hysteresis to 12MB or tighten batching concurrency to avoid simultaneous spikes.

jia: small test plan: 1) for one canary host set kv_hysteresis_mb=12 2) pin batching window to 12ms 3) re-run perf capture for 10m. we should see evict_ratio drop and L2 misses fall.

ops-bot: scheduled draining check on gpu-7c: will move <5% traffic while we flip config.

alex: applied kv_hysteresis_mb=12 and batching window=12ms on canary-pool-7 at 03:30. initial numbers: throughput back up ~10%, evict_ratio for shard-3 -> 0.48, mem delta stable ~+1GB.

perf-bot: post-change automated profile (03:30-03:40):
perf-bot: ```
- L2 miss rate back to baseline +/-1%
- stall_cycles down 9%
- kernel_time% for softmax/transpose down ~7%
```

maria: great. can we also run a calibration sensitivity sweep? we need to know safe quant calibration changes that keep KV footprint within hysteresis margins. add a rule to release notes: "calibration must include kv footprint delta estimate".

rowan: agreed — long-term fix: 1) add kv_delta estimate to calibration artifacts 2) make hysteresis auto-scale with observed max per-token footprint by model/seq 3) add a canary gating rule: if predicted kv_delta > 8MB, block wide rollout.

jia: i'll own the sweep and the gating rule PR. will include a small perf test harness to simulate concurrent tiny/long seq mix.

alex: thanks. summary: transient throughput drop caused by kv eviction hysteresis + batching concurrency interacting with NF4 calibration footprint; mitigation bumped hysteresis and reduced batching window, improved metrics. next: calibration artifact change + gating + automated tests. :thumbsup:

rowan: leaving notes for postmortem doc: add timeline, per-shard counters, perf profiles, and the simple reproducer script.

alex: tagging @maria for release note line and @ops-bot to re-open canary if everything remains stable.

ops-bot: canary traffic restored to normal at 03:48. monitoring alerts cleared by 03:56.

alex: closing thread, will copy key logs into the incident repo.
